Robot Doctor Mechanisms

A motor won't spin

One motor does nothing, or only hums. Below are the 5 most common causes on FTC robots, ordered from most to least likely, with how to check and fix each one.

Skip the guesswork — run the interactive diagnosisAbout 6 quick questions narrow this list down to your robot's actual problem.

Quick checks first

  • Does telemetry show the code sending non-zero power to it? Print motor.getPower() (and the mode) in your loop.
  • Does the motor hum or get hot without moving? Listen and carefully feel the motor after trying to run it.
  • With power off, does the mechanism move smoothly by hand through its whole range? Backdrive it slowly. Feel for tight spots, grinding, or places it catches.
  • Does the motor work if you plug it into a different port (and update the config)? Move the motor to a spare port you know works and change the configuration to match.
  • Does the error say "Unable to find a hardware device with the name ..."? The red error text at the bottom of the Driver Station.
  • Does the error mention TargetPositionNotSet? Shows up when switching to RUN_TO_POSITION too early.

Common causes and how to fix them

1 The code never actually powers it

The motor is configured, but the code sets power 0, sets it in the wrong mode, or the button logic never runs.

How to fix it 5 min

  1. Add telemetry that prints the power you are sending and the motor's mode.
  2. With RUN_TO_POSITION, the motor only moves if you set a target, switch to RUN_TO_POSITION, and set power above 0.
  3. Watch for two parts of the code fighting, like one line setting power and another setting 0 later in the same loop.
RUN_TO_POSITION in the right order
arm.setTargetPosition(1120);                      // 1. target first
arm.setMode(DcMotor.RunMode.RUN_TO_POSITION);     // 2. then the mode
arm.setPower(0.6);                                // 3. then power > 0

Sources: GM0 · Common software issues · GM0 · Encoders

2 Motor power wire or port problem

The motor's power plug is loose, in the wrong port, or the port is damaged.

How to fix it 10 min

  1. Follow the motor wire to the hub and push the power plug (JST VH) firmly in. Make sure it is in the port number the configuration says.
  2. Swap the motor into a port you know works. If it runs there, the old port or its configuration is the problem.
  3. To check a port, run it at full power and measure across the port pins with a multimeter. You should see roughly battery voltage. No voltage means the port is damaged (REV has a repair service).

Sources: REV · Testing a motor port · GM0 · Wiring guide

3 Mechanism is jammed or overloaded

If the mechanism binds or the load is too heavy for the gearing, the motor stalls. It hums, heats up, and drains the battery.

How to fix it 15 min

  1. Power off and move the mechanism by hand through its full range. It should move smoothly with no tight spots.
  2. Feel the motor after a run. Hot means it is stalling or working far too hard.
  3. Check for over-tightened chain or belt, misaligned shafts, screws hitting things, or a hard stop the code keeps pushing into.
  4. If the load really is too heavy, add reduction or a second motor. The RoboCodex gear ratio calculator helps size it.

Sources: GM0 · Building tips · FTC Docs · Power management

4 Name in code doesn't match the configuration

"Unable to find a hardware device with the name ..." means the string in hardwareMap.get is not exactly the name in the active configuration.

How to fix it 5 min

  1. Open the configuration on the Driver Station and compare names letter by letter. They are case sensitive ("leftDrive" is not "LeftDrive").
  2. Make sure the configuration you edited is the active one (its name shows on the DS main screen) and that you saved it.
  3. Watch for trailing spaces in config names.

Sources: FTC Docs · Troubleshooting common issues

5 RUN_TO_POSITION set before a target

TargetPositionNotSetException means you switched to RUN_TO_POSITION before calling setTargetPosition.

How to fix it 2 min

  1. Call setTargetPosition first, then setMode(RUN_TO_POSITION), then setPower.
Right order
motor.setTargetPosition(1120);
motor.setMode(DcMotor.RunMode.RUN_TO_POSITION);
motor.setPower(0.5);

Sources: GM0 · Common software issues

Related problems

  • Slides or arm sag, slip, or won't hold
  • Arm or slide shakes, overshoots, or runs away
  • Chain or belt skips or falls off
  • Something works, then loosens or slips over time
